Package errorMsg

Class CompError

java.lang.Object
errorMsg.CompMessage
errorMsg.CompError
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<CompMessage>
public class CompError extends CompMessage
Represent an error in the compiler. Use the static methods below to reate an error. Don't use the CompError constructor.

    • DuplicateClass

      public static CompError DuplicateClass(String name)
      An error for when two classes are declared with the same name.
      Example:
      class ThisClass { }
      class ThisClass { }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the duplicate class.

    • DuplicateField

      public static CompError DuplicateField(String name)
      An error representing a duplicate field.
      The field can be of a different type.
      Example:
      class ThisClass
      {
          int x;
          double x;
      }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the field.

    • DuplicateMethod

      public static CompError DuplicateMethod(String name)
      An error representing a duplicate method in the same class.
      Example:
      class ThisClass
      {
          int foo() { return 0; }
          double foo() { return 0.0; }
      }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the duplicate method.

    • IllegalSuperclass

      public static CompError IllegalSuperclass(String name)
      An error representing a class that is either "String" or "RunMain".

      class String { }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the class (should be either "String" or "RunMain")

    • UndefinedSuperclass

      public static CompError UndefinedSuperclass(String name)
      An error for a class that extends an undefined class.
      Example:
      class thisClass extends DoesNotExist { }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the superclass that does not exist.

    • InheritanceCycle

      public static CompError InheritanceCycle(String name)
      An error if an inheritance cycle is detected.
      Example:
      class A extends B { }
      class B extends C { }
      class C extends A { }
      Parameters:
      name - the name of the class where the inheritance cycle was discovered.

    • Subtype

      public static CompError Subtype(Type t1, Type t2)
      An error for when one type should be a subtype, but isn't.
      Example:
      class A { ... }
      class B extends A { ... }
      class C { ... }
      ...
      A c = new C();
      since C is not a subtype of A, this is not allowed.
      Parameters:
      t1 - the type that should be a subtype (C in our example)
      t2 - the type that should be a supertype (A in our example)

    • Assignment

      public static CompError Assignment()
      An error for if the left hand side of an assignment is not assignable.
      Example: 2 + 2 = x;

    • ArrayType

      public static CompError ArrayType()
      An error for an array subscript used on an expression that isn't an array.
      Example: 4[6] = 2;

    • IncompatibleType

      public static CompError IncompatibleType(Type t1, Type t2)
      An error for if two types are not compatible.
      Two types t1 and t2 are compatible if one is a subtype of the other, but the order doesn't matter.

      Example: 4 == "hi";
      Example: int x == "hi";
      Example: 4 istanceof String;
      Parameters:
      t1 - the type of the left hand side
      t2 - the type of the right hand side

    • UndefinedMethod

      public static CompError UndefinedMethod(String methName, Type t)
      An error for if a method isn't defined.
      This has to be in typechecking because we have to know the type of the expression to see if the method exists.

      Example:
      class Empty { }
      ...
      Empty x = new Empty();
      x.doMethod();
      Parameters:
      methName - the name of the method
      t - the type of the object that is supposed to have the method

    • ParameterMismatch

      public static CompError ParameterMismatch(String methName, int argSize, int paramSize)
      An error if the wrong number of arguments are used in a method call.
      Example
      class ThisClass { void foo(int a) { } }
      ...
      ThisClass x = new ThisClass();
      x.foo(1,2,3);
      Parameters:
      methName - the name of the method
      argSize - the number of arguments used in the method call
      paramSize - the number of parameters in the method definition

    • UndefinedField

      public static CompError UndefinedField(String fieldName, Type t)
      An error for a field access for an object where the class doesn't define the field.
      Example:
      class Empty { }
      ...
      Empty x = new Empty();
      x.someField = 4;
      Parameters:
      fieldName - the name of the field
      t - the type of class that is supposed to have the field.

    • TypeMismatch

      public static CompError TypeMismatch(Type t1, Type t2)
      An error for when a type needs to be exactly int or bool.
      Example: 4 + new Ostrich();

    • NewRunMain

      public static CompError NewRunMain()
      An error for someone trying to make a new RunMain object.
      Example: new RunMain()

    • ReturnOverride

      public static CompError ReturnOverride()
      An error for when the return types for overriding methods don't match.
      Example:
      class A
      {
          int foo() { ... }
      }
      class B extends A
      {
          double foo() { ... }
      }

    • ArgTypeOverride

      public static CompError ArgTypeOverride()
      An error for if an argument type in an overridden method doesn't match the base method.
      Example:
      class A
      {
          void foo(int x) { ... }
      }
      class B extends A
      {
          void foo(double x) { ... }
      }

    • NumArgsOverride

      public static CompError NumArgsOverride()
      An error for if the number of arguments doesn't match the number in the base method.
      Example:
      class A
      {
          void foo(int x) { ... }
      }
      class B extends A
      {
          void foo(int x, double y) { ... }
      }

    • FirstLabelSwitch

      public static CompError FirstLabelSwitch()
      An error for if the first statement in a switch isn't a case or default.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
          int x = 4;
          case 4:
              break;
      }

    • LabelAfterBreakSwitch

      public static CompError LabelAfterBreakSwitch()
      An error for if there is a statment after a break that is not a label.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
          case 4:
              break;
              int x = 4;
      }

    • EndBreakSwitch

      public static CompError EndBreakSwitch()
      An error for if the last statement in a switch isn't a break statement.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
      ...
          default:
              int x = 4;
      }

    • DuplicateDefaultSwitch

      public static CompError DuplicateDefaultSwitch()
      An error for if there is a duplicate default statement in a switch.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
      ...
          default:
              int x = 4;
      }

    • DuplicateKeySwitch

      public static CompError DuplicateKeySwitch()
      An error for if there is a duplicate key in a case statement.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
      ...
          case 4:
              break;
          case 4:
              break;
      }

    • NonConstantCase

      public static CompError NonConstantCase()
      An error for if the expression in a case statement is non-constant.
      Example:
      switch(x) {
      ...
          case x + 4:
              break;
      }
